key_insight: A hybrid quantum-classical Benders framework jointly optimizes bidirectional EV charging and trip assignments while limiting auxiliary-qubit overhead.
engineering_relevance: The approach supports EV fleet scheduling that coordinates transportation needs with vehicle-to-grid energy exchange.
method: Decompose the joint scheduling problem using hybrid quantum-classical Benders optimization.
Use logic-based conflict cuts requiring near-zero auxiliary qubits.
Apply a sparse recursive state-of-charge formulation to reduce constraint-matrix density by a factor of T/3.
evidence_signal: The framework recovers MILP-optimal solutions on benchmark instances with a low auxiliary-qubit budget and runs a small instance end-to-end on IBM quantum hardware.
watch_item: The small hardware proof of concept does not establish quantum speedup or scalability to operational fleet sizes.
paper_title: Quantum-Classical Framework for the Joint Optimization of Bidirectional EV Charging and Trip Assignment
